Remedy Robotics raises $62 million to prepare pivotal N1 trials

The Series B supports endovascular robotics and planned testing with the University of California; N1 is not available for sale or clinical use.

PR Newswire / Remedy Robotics ↗16 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Financing the next development stage

Remedy Robotics announced a $62 million Series B led by DCVC on November 16. The funding will support planned pivotal clinical testing with the University of California, prototype placements with partners and progress toward potential FDA approval. These are development objectives, not approvals or successful trial outcomes already achieved.

Robotics combined with imaging

N1 combines robotic equipment and software for endovascular intervention. Development includes preoperative image analysis, case simulation and real-time registration between 3D and 2D images. The intended operating modes include onsite control, remote operation and autonomous functions. Each mode needs its own supporting evaluation; evidence for remote control does not validate full autonomy.

The system remains under development

The release explicitly states that N1 is not currently available for sale or clinical use in any jurisdiction. Remote procedures reported in 2025 are development milestones, not authorization for general use. The next evidence should come from clinical testing and regulatory review; financing alone does not establish safety or effectiveness.
